# Plan and Implement

## Change Summary

Tightened the schema-2→3 save migration in `crates/tank_core/src/save.rs` so malformed legacy saves now fail explicitly instead of being coerced. The migration now requires positive geometry dimensions/fill height, rejects negative substrate depths and substrate columns deeper than fill height, and errors on non-positive gross or net water volume before rescaling dissolved totals. In `crates/tank_core/tests/save_load.rs`, I added a shared malformed-save assertion helper and regression tests covering negative fill height, negative substrate depth, and substrate depth exceeding fill height, alongside the existing missing-field failure case.

## Steps

1. [Completed] Inspected the existing v2→v3 migration path to identify every malformed numeric case that was still being clamped or zero-scaled instead of rejected: non-positive geometry, negative substrate depth, excessive substrate depth, and non-positive derived water volumes.
2. [Completed] Patched `crates/tank_core/src/save.rs` to validate those legacy geometry/depth inputs explicitly and return `SimError::SchemaMigration` with descriptive messages before any dissolved-total rescaling occurs.
3. [Completed] Expanded `crates/tank_core/tests/save_load.rs` with focused malformed-legacy regression coverage and reran targeted save/load plus lint validation.

## Validation Evidence

- `cargo test -p tank_core --test save_load` passed: 18 tests passed, including the new malformed schema-v2 cases for negative fill height, negative substrate depth, and substrate depth exceeding fill height.
- `cargo clippy -p tank_core --tests -- -D warnings` passed with no warnings.

## Outstanding Risks

- Known unrelated branch regression carried forward from prior validation: `cargo test -p tank_core --test shrimp_population hatch_produces_juveniles -- --exact` was previously failing on this branch with TAN around 2.169 mg/L and no juvenile hatch; this migration amendment did not address or revalidate it.
- Known unrelated architectural issue carried forward from prior review: `Engine::step_hours` still calls `enforce_invariants(&mut self.state)` before returning some invariant errors, so a rejected step can still mutate live state.
